master: Create a NEW photorealistic Chinese elm bonsai inspired by the real museum tree reference's botanical anatomy, not a copy. Natural irregular winding tapered trunk, subtle patchy warm grey/tan elm bark, visible connected fine branch ramification, root flare anchored in soil. Avoid repetitive sinusoidal S bends and stacked pompom/topiary pads. Asymmetric broad graceful crown with small serrated oval leaves arranged along slender twigs, separated airy foliage masses with clear gaps and soft restrained green tones. Strong trunk movement and modest irregular bends like a real hand-trained living elm. Shallow oval muted warm grey ceramic pot with small feet, sparse moss and granular earth. Square 1536 composition, pot spans x22%-78%, pot bottom y94%, soil y83%, mature crown top y8%, crown x12%-88%; camera locked at slightly above pot rim, entire pot visible. Soft neutral studio photography, true transparent alpha background, no table/wall/stand, no text, no flowers, no CGI. One mature bonsai, the master final keyframe of a seed-to-bonsai growth storyboard.
